Nine people were killed in the shooting at the Greek Orthodox church last month
A Jordanian court has sentenced three men to death by hanging for carrying out a fatal mass shooting on a church last month.
The attack on 23 October killed nine people and injured 34 others who had been attending a Christian funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate.
Jordan's Armed Forces said in a statement on Sunday that the men had been convicted of committing "terrorist acts", as well as possessing weapons, "promoting the ideas of a terrorist organisation" and "conspiracy to commit terrorist acts".
The three men - two Jordanian brothers and their brother-in-law - fled the scene of the attack and were arrested three days later. They have not been publicly identified.
Karak is home to a sizeable Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom.
CCTV footage from the day of the attack showed three men holding guns approaching and firing on St George's church in the village of Hmoud.
A second video showed dead and wounded people lying on the ground amid chaotic scenes at the church.
It is still unclear why the attackers chose to target that specific church.
Shortly after the attack, Jordan's King Abdullah II wrote on X: "The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation.
"Those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets have no chance in the face of our unity."
The three men fled the scene of the shooting and were later located inside an abandoned house in Karak governorate, south of the capital, Amman.
They refused to surrender and opened fire on security forces, who returned fire and wounded all three of them , the Public Security Directorate said at the time. No security personnel were hurt in the shootout.
King Abdullah praised security forces for chasing the suspects "to the very end".
The week after the Karak shooting, Jordan struck what its military said were "terrorist organisations" in Syria in retaliation to the church attack.
Syrian health officials told state media that five people, including women, children and an elderly man, were killed in the strike on a village in the southern Daraa province. Jordan said its fighter jets had killed and wounded "several terrorists" without giving further details.
Jordan said it had co-ordinated with the Syrian government, but Syria said it had not been notified in advance.
Executions in Jordan are carried out by hanging. The kingdom previously observed an unofficial ban on executions from 2006 to 2014, and another pause from 2017 until June this year.

It's not about technology for its own sake. It's about being able to implement your ideas.
Turbo Pascal 3 for MS-DOS was released in September 1986. Being version 3, there were lesser releases prior to it and flashier ones after, but 3 was a solid representation of the Turbo Pascal experience: a full Pascal compiler, including extensions that it made it practical for commercial use, tightly integrated with an editor. And the whole thing was lightning fast, orders of magnitude faster at building projects than Microsoft's compilers.
The entire Turbo Pascal 3.02 executable--the compiler and IDE--was 39,731 bytes. How does that stack up in 2011 terms? Here are some things that Turbo Pascal is smaller than, as of October 30, 2011:
The image of the white iPhone 4S at apple.com (190,157 bytes).
Various vim quick reference cards as PDFs. ( This one is 47,508 bytes.)
The compiled code for the Erlang R14B02 parser ( erl_parse.beam , 286,324 bytes).
(If you liked this, you might like A Personal History of Compilation Speed .)

A senior Hamas figure who helped plan and oversee the 7 October 2023 attack on Israel has been killed in an Israeli airstrike, officials in Israel and Gaza have said.
Samir Abu Younis, the newly appointed commander of the Rafah Brigade, was killed on Saturday in Al-Mawasi in the southern Gaza Strip, according to Hamas's Al-Qassam Brigades military wing.
A local Hamas official confirmed Younis's death. The Israeli military said it had targeted him and that prior to the strike "steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians".
Eyewitnesses in Gaza said four missiles struck a tent in the Al-Waha camp, which shelters hundreds of displaced people in Al-Mawasi, causing a fire to break out.
A medical source at Nasser Hospital in the southern city of Khan Younis said three injured people had arrived there, as well as a dead body.
The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) and Israel's security agency, the ISA, confirmed in a statement on Telegram that it had "eliminated" Younis.
Describing him as a "central figure among Hamas's senior figures", it said he had "acted with the aim of trying to restore the strength of the brigade and the Hamas terrorist organisation".
It added: "Younis directed the brigade's terrorists to advance and carry out terror attacks against Israeli civilians and IDF troops."
Al-Qassam Brigades wrote on Telegram that Younis had "participated in numerous high-profile operations and resisted enemy incursions", and was "one of the most important commanders involved in planning and overseeing the 7 October attack".
Younis, 53, had been in his position since 15 September, following the death of the brigade's previous commander, Nael Abu Obeid.
He joined Hamas' armed wing in 1991 and held several senior operational roles before becoming commander. His funeral will be held on Sunday afternoon in Khan Younis, Hamas said.
The Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed an 251 others taken hostage, triggered the most recent war in Gaza.
Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in the Palestinian territory, the health ministry there says.
Though a ceasefire was reached last October, Israel has continued strikes it says are targeting remaining Hamas militants, which it argues it has the right to do under the terms of the ceasefire agreement.
More than 1,640 people have been killed in Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire, according to the territory's health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.
Update November 15: An earlier version of this article referred to Israel carrying out 'occasional' strikes in Gaza following a ceasefire in October 2025. This word has been removed to better reflect the frequency of Israeli strikes on Gaza since the ceasefire.

Ukraine’s NATO ambition has always been a red line for the Kremlin. Giving up territory has been a no-no for Ukraine. Will they make compromises?
The United States has pitched a new pathway for Ukraine to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), an aspiration that Kyiv has long held as a means to guarantee its defence against Russia, almost five years into their war.
But the administration of President Donald Trump has suggested that Ukraine would need to agree to give up all of the Donbas region in the country’s east, which Russian President Vladimir Putin has demanded as one of his conditions for ending the war.
The idea, according to Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, was communicated to him by Trump’s negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at the latest round of US-mediated peace talks between Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, last week.
After the Abu Dhabi round of talks, Kushner and Witkoff met Putin in Moscow on Thursday, then briefed Zelenskyy in Dublin, before a meeting of European leaders in the Irish capital on Friday.
Ukraine applied to become a member of NATO in September 2022, seeking to fortify its borders with Russia.
But the Kremlin has repeatedly said Ukraine becoming a member of NATO would demand “a harsh response” from Russia.
So will Washington’s latest pitch be acceptable to both Ukraine and Russia?
On Saturday, Zelenskyy told reporters that Kushner and Witkoff had suggested that Ukraine could become a NATO member if it ceded control of Donbas in the east.
He said, “The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?'”
“NATO is back on the agenda” since it is part of an “extremely difficult” conversation between Ukraine and Russia which would determine the future of European security, Zelenskyy said.
Putin has been against Ukraine’s NATO membership and has demanded that the alliance pull back its troops from countries bordering Russia.
“This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations,” Zelenskyy said.
“Real security in Europe means the EU [European Union] and NATO. That’s it. There is no other security in Europe.”
Ian Lesser, distinguished fellow at the German Marshall Fund of the US, told Al Jazeera that Washington’s proposal, if accurate, is significant because it articulates very directly an approach long current in US administration circles that Ukraine should be prepared to make territorial concessions in the service of a settlement.
“The NATO element seems very doubtful. Surely attractive to Ukraine, but [it is] hard to imagine Moscow agreeing to this. And some NATO members will be doubtful too,” he said.
Chris Featherstone, a political scientist from the University of York in the United Kingdom, argued that the proposal was a major departure from previously held positions.
“The US has been very cautious about getting further involved in Ukraine, with the Biden administration giving military support, but clearly opposing any ideas of Western involvement on the ground. Trump has seemed to be very sympathetic to the Russian cause, and has had significant blow-ups with Zelenskyy, so this proposal is certainly a surprise,” he noted.
He told Al Jazeera that offering NATO membership in a peace settlement would give significant support to Ukraine should Russia reinitiate the conflict in the future.
“In the light of Trump’s repeated attacks on NATO, this could be seen as a recommitment to the alliance. However, there would be questions over whether Trump could bring other NATO allies to support the proposal,” he added.
Ukraine applied to become a NATO member in September 2022, just months after Russia’s full-scale invasion of the country.
Since then, Zelenskyy, his officials and Ukrainians around the world have been lobbying NATO nations to speed up Kyiv’s accession process.
But NATO members remain divided over offering Ukraine alliance membership amid an ongoing war despite a broad consensus to signal strong support for Kyiv.
NATO members bordering Russia, like Lithuania and Poland, have been most enthusiastic about backing Ukraine’s ambitions. Several other nations in the alliance have also been supportive of an expedited process for Kyiv to join, amid concerns about corruption in Ukraine and while seeking an end to the war with Russia as a condition for the country to become a NATO member.
But under President Trump, the US has been far less receptive to Ukraine’s calls for NATO membership. Trump has publicly told Ukraine to give up on hopes of joining the alliance.
Yet, while the new proposal from Witkoff and Kushner revives Ukraine’s hopes of joining NATO, it demands a compromise that no government in Kyiv can easily make.
On Saturday, Zelenskyy told reporters that the prospect of Ukraine joining NATO in exchange for ceding territory had not been raised by members of the alliance before and reiterated that Kyiv would not give up any of its territories.
But he said if Ukraine received a peace deal which included security guarantees, the right to maintain a strong and well-funded Ukrainian army, and funds to rebuild the country, then he would hold a national referendum on the question of ceding territory in exchange for NATO membership.
Featherstone noted that Ukraine has been fighting for a long time and has consistently maintained that it will not relinquish its territory in a peace deal.
“The proposal from the Trump administration is clearly an attempt to test this Ukrainian position, in an effort to confront the impasse,” he said.
“NATO membership would give a level of security that Ukraine would likely welcome. However, this would be a big sacrifice of territory and sovereignty. After years of Trump’s questioning of the NATO commitment, Ukraine would need a strong statement of commitment to its defence should they be considering any proposal like this,” he added.
The Kremlin has not yet responded to the latest US proposal.
But it has maintained a strict position that Ukraine’s NATO membership is a red line for Moscow and a direct threat to Russia’s national security. In fact, Putin has also cited the issue of Ukraine’s NATO aspirations as one reason why Russia launched its war in 2022.
Despite Kushner and Witkoff’s meetings with Putin, the Kremlin has shown little appetite for a change in that position. Moscow has continued, throughout the war, to demand that Ukraine abandon its NATO ambitions and maintain a neutral and demilitarised status. Russia has also firmly opposed any deployment of Western troops or peacekeepers on Ukrainian soil.
In addition to demanding that Ukraine give up its NATO dreams, Moscow has also insisted that Ukraine should cede sovereignty over the Donbas region, in addition to parts of Zaporizhia and Kherson provinces that Russia already occupies.
Just as the new US proposal asks Ukraine to give up some territory in return for a NATO seat, it offers Russia a bargain — withdraw its red line on Ukraine’s NATO membership and get the Donbas in exchange.
The region in eastern Ukraine has historically been the country’s industrial heartland and is therefore a critical economic engine.
A majority of people in the Donbas identify as ethnically Ukrainian, but a minority identifies as ethnically Russian. The Russian language is also widely spoken in the region — a legacy of Russian migration there in the 19th century and then under the Soviet Union.
Russia accuses Ukraine of discriminating against Russian-speaking and ethnically Russian people in the Donbas and has used this claim to justify its demand that Kyiv hand over the region to Moscow.
The region consists of the provinces of Luhansk and Donetsk. Since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, Russia has occupied almost all of Luhansk and most of Donetsk. ‘We think dialogue is a good thing,’ Australian PM says after German chancellor urges the US to work with Europe for peace in Ukraine
Australia has endorsed this week’s historic summit between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in China, even as European leaders warn that the US president must not make major concessions over the war in Ukraine.
The three-way summit is planned to take place in Shenzhen, where the leaders will gather for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) meeting. The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , has warned the talks must not lead to a redistribution of influence among world powers or the abandonment of his country, more than four years into the war sparked by Putin’s full-scale invasion.
Speaking in Manila on Sunday, the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese , welcomed the talks taking place but insisted the clear message to Putin was that the war should end.
Albanese, in the Philippines before a meeting of Quad leaders and talks with south-east Asian leaders at the Asean summit, left open the possibility of joining an Apec group photo with Putin if China wished for it to go ahead.
“We think that dialogue is a good thing and we await the outcome of that dialogue,” he said.
“It’s obviously quite significant, the fact that President Trump will be at Asean as well as at Apec, and that we’ll have a Quad leaders meeting as well.
“We want to see something constructive come out of that, including we want to see a de-escalation in the conflicts around the world.”
German’s chancellor, Friedrich Merz , expressed hesitation about the talks at a meeting of EU leaders on Friday.
“I want to state our message to the US very clearly once again: please, no surprises,” he said. “Stay on Team Europe and Team Ukraine , and let us work together for a genuine peace in Ukraine.”
France’s president, Emmanuel Macron , warned against forcing “an unjust peace” on Ukraine and, by extension, all of Europe.
“That is the spirit of defeat,” Macron said. “That is a recipe for another war.”
The meeting has been compared to a 1945 summit at Yalta , in southern Crimea, when then US president, Franklin D Roosevelt, Britain’s Winston Churchill and the Soviet leader Joseph Stalin carved up influence across war-ravaged Europe. Zelenskyy has warned that the meeting must not turn into “Yalta 2, 3, 4”.
The historian Timothy Garton Ash has called the trilateral summit, organised after a proposal by Putin last month, “a sort of parody” of Yalta, even as analysts say decisions on the future of Ukraine or China’s ambitions to take control of Taiwan without their involvement is unlikely.
Albanese said the summit would not undercut a growing push by countries including Australia and Canada for middle powers to have greater influence in world affairs.
“We’ll continue to engage with like-minded countries,” he said. “There are two super powers in the world.
“What’s important about the struggle of the people of Ukraine is that they’re not just standing up for their own sovereignty; they’re standing up for the international rule of law.”
Asked if he would join the so-called “family photo” of Apec leaders if Putin took part, Albanese said he would consider the wishes of China as the host nation. But he said the Russian president should know Australia’s opposition to the invasion.
“If he’s in a room where I am, I’m sure they’ll hear my contribution,” Albanese said.
After the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting, Australia’s Penny Wong joined with European and Canadian counterparts to avoid a group photo . It was cancelled by US officials when a third of participants declined to stand alongside the Russian foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov.
Albanese signed a new defence agreement with the Philippines on Sunday, visiting the supply ship HMAS Stalwart in the Port of Manila. Australia is helping to strengthen the Philippines’ defensive capability against Chinese aggression.
More freedom-of-navigation naval exercises are planned in an attempt to counter Beijing’s efforts to influence the South and East China seas.

Joana Rosa and four other opposition candidates face off against President Jose Maria Neves, who wants a second term.
Voters have begun casting their ballots in Cape Verde, where President Jose Maria Neves is facing off against the West African island nation’s first female presidential candidate, Joana Rosa, in a vote hinging on slowing down persistent emigration.
More than 300,000 people are eligible to vote on Sunday from 8am to 6pm (09:00 GMT to 19:00 GMT) and will choose from six presidential candidates in a country known for its stability in the politically volatile region.
Neves, a member of the country’s oldest political party, the African Party for the Independence of Cape Verde (PAICV), is tipped to be the favourite but faces his strongest challenger in Rosa of the Movement for Democracy party.
The 66-year-old served as prime minister for 15 years and became president in 2021. His party won 37 of 72 parliamentary seats in May, allowing Neves to appoint Francisco Carvalho, then mayor of the capital, Praia, as prime minister.
Rosa, an opposition candidate and former justice minister, is the first woman to run for president since independence in 1975. Her party governed for 10 years before the May vote.
The country runs a hybrid parliamentary-presidential system of government that sees the president enjoy veto authority and a mediating role.
Cape Verde, a tourism haven located off the coast of Senegal, gained global fame this year after its men’s football team battled with much bigger nations to reach the World Cup knockout stages. In April, a cruise ship sailing off its coast was struck by a hantavirus outbreak.
Emigration has long been a problem because of a dearth of jobs. The archipelago has more people living in the diaspora than the 500,000 people residing on its islands. Most are in Portugal, its former coloniser, and the United States.
Nearly 77,000 diaspora Cape Verdeans are registered to vote at embassies abroad.
Neves has promised to organise a youth summit to address emigration if he is elected to a second term. Rosa, meanwhile, called for a government that allows young people “to build their futures here at home and prevent the continued exodus of young Cape Verdeans abroad”.
But many voters feel distant from the political class over concerns that it doesn’t understand their daily difficulties, Roselma Evora, a professor of political science and gender studies at the University of Cabo Verde, told The Associated Press news agency.
Candidates must clinch more than 50 percent of the vote to win, or the top two candidates will face a run-off vote on November 29.

The Port of New Orleans is suing the owners and managers of a tanker that crashed into a cruise ship docked there on Friday.
The port is claiming the tanker is at fault for the collision that saw more than 100 passengers being rescued from the Mississippi River and caused more than $1m (£756,000) in damage, according to court documents.
The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one was unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi".
The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering."
The paddlewheel cruise ship, American Heritage, was left on its side and partially submerged in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt on Friday afternoon.
The court documents added that the port terminal had been "significantly damaged" in the incident.
The tanker, the M/V Atlantic Asphalt, its owner Nave Shipping SA and its management company Thome Ship Management Pte Ltd are all named in the lawsuit filed in federal court on Friday in the Eastern District of Louisiana.
Officials are still investigating the full extent of the damage from the crash, as well as the cause, but the lawsuit says the port is looking for money to cover clean-up, inspections, repairs and other expenses.
Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans
The lawsuit requests that the tanker be seized and sold to pay for the damage. It also alleges that the collision "occurred as a result of the negligence, gross negligence, fault or carelessness" of the ship and operating companies.
It alleges that the tanker and companies failed "to use all available means to avoid the risk" of colliding with the riverboat.
Nave Shipping is a subsidiary of the China State Shipbuilding Corporation. BBC has contacted the latter for comment.
Thome Ship Management has also been contacted. The firm said in a statement on Saturday that the crew of the Atlantic Asphalt were safe and accounted for.
"OSM Thome is fully complying with the local authorities as they carry out the necessary investigations," it said.
The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said at a news conference on Saturday that the tanker's data recorder, which preserves information like the boat's speed and audio, has been recovered as part of the investigation.
A preliminary report about the incident will be released in 30 days, but a final report could take 18 to 24 months.
There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority.
Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort.
The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway at the time.
If you were in the area at the time of the incident, please get in touch.

Cape Verde goes to the polls on Sunday in an election that could see the African island nation appoint its first ever female leader. Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent Jose Maria Neves, who is the country's fifth president since it became independent from Portugal in 1975.
Cape Verde could elect its first woman president Sunday as former Justice Minister Joana Rosa challenges incumbent Jose Maria Neves, who is seeking a second term.
Six candidates are competing, with a runoff scheduled for Nov. 29 if no candidate receives more than half the votes.
Rosa, backed by the opposition Movement for Democracy, is the first woman to run for president since independence from Portugal in 1975. Women have held senior cabinet posts, but Cape Verde has never had a female prime minister or president.
In Cape Verde’s parliamentary system, the prime minister directs government policy and holds most executive authority. The president’s role is largely symbolic, although the directly elected head of state can veto legislation.
The Atlantic island nation off West Africa , home to about half a million people, has a record of peaceful transfers of power and competitive elections in a region where that is rare. Nearly 77,000 Cape Verdeans abroad are registered to vote, almost a fifth of the total electorate.
Many voters feel distant from their leaders and want a president who understands their daily difficulties, while limited economic prospects were driving young people to seek opportunities abroad, said Roselma Évora, a professor of political science and gender studies at the University of Cabo Verde.
Neves, who won in 2021 with about 52% of the vote, has pledged to build cross-party support to improve housing, healthcare and education, create jobs and raise wages.
Incumbency gives Neves greater visibility, including among overseas voters, Evora said.

Rosa’s candidacy challenges traditional expectations of women’s roles in a society that remains “very patriarchal", Évora said.

We are in the middle of the Second ReNESance (the first one is the one that saved the video game industry in North America). The combined decades of research and knowledge on how the venerable little NES works have produced a true cornucopia of games. We are all lucky to be here to witness it.
I am always happy to inform video game fans that the Nintendo Entertainment System is still receiving lots and lots of new third-party games.
In alphabetical order, because I refuse to rank them, here are 25 of my favourite modern NES games. Almost all can be obtained digitally, usually from the developer or publisher, most for a modest fee. Digital NES downloads are cheap! Most of these can also be obtained as physical cartridges for the true hi-fi experience on original hardware.
Made by 8-bit Slasher who has been honing his skills in other horror games for the NES, All Hell Unleashed is an extensive love letter to the horror slashers of the 1980s and 1990s. There is an underlying story about an evil cult that is trying to resurrect something or other, but that’s just an excuse plot so that you can fight Jaws, Freddy, Jason, Ghostface and others. It works surprisingly well. You can select your favourite horror movie from a stage-select screen to do your platforming as you fight the forces of evil, culminating in the boss fights where the villain of each horror franchise swoops in for a mano-a-mano . The platforming feels good, and the boss fights function as set pieces showcasing the real villains we are here to see in their 8-bit glory.
Finally Jason dons a better outfit on the NES than that silly purple jumpsuit!
After each classic horror villain is defeated, it is time to take on the cult itself for one final showdown. Definitely a spine-tingling adventure!
Alwa’s Awakening was originally a PC game made with pseudo-NES limitations (and in the case of the music, with actual NES limitations, as the developer used Famitracker to compose all of the music). If it doesn’t feel like a classic NES game and instead plays more like a modern indie Metroidvania, that’s because it is.
In the game, you play as Zoe, a girl who likes video games and one day awakens in the mystical land of Alwa, a place from one of her games. Your task is to guide Zoe through an adventure in Alwa where she will uncover power-ups that open up new avenues of adventure. Typical Metroidvania stuff, although a bit shorter than most games in the genre. The PC-to-NES port of this game was handled by my good friend Brad Smith of Lizard fame. He made a couple of interesting YouTube videos describing the process.
The game looks absolutely gorgeous for the NES, and its Famitracker-composed soundtrack made it through the porting process completely unscathed. There was a limited physical edition that today is only available via secondhand markets. If you can grab a copy, it’s a very high-quality production. This is some of the best stuff made for the system.
Anguna is an NES game with an interesting lineage. It was originally made in 2008 for the Game Boy Advance as essentially the same game, but a bit more to the standards of the GBA. Then it was successively ported to the Nintendo DS, the Atari 2600, and finally the NES.
The Atari 2600-to-NES port was done fairly faithfully, which means that the design decisions necessary for the Atari also made it into the NES port. This means, for example, no more than two enemies per screen and always of the same type. This sort of restriction isn’t unheard of in the NES, though. The very popular NES Double Dragon port also has the same limitation. The game design makes up for it and overall results in an enjoyable experience. And isn’t that what making and playing modern NES games is all about? An interesting experience made with strict hardware limitations.
So what is Anguna? At its most basic, it’s a Zelda-like. You walk around screens, you grab new tools, your tools open new paths for exploration, you use the tools to fight monsters, with the most common tool in question being your trusty sword. You are a nameless warrior who is notably NOT called “Anguna” on a quest to defeat the goblin king. Usual bare-bones plot.
Most might consider this game to be short, but I would say it’s sleek and streamlined. It doesn’t do much, but what it does it does well.
Oh, one very important upgrade that the game got during the 2600-to-NES conversion: rockin’ enemy portraits in gorgeous 8-bit pixel art!
Blazing Rangers is single-screen arcade firefighting co-op action! The firefighting genre is under-explored in video games and Blazing Rangers manages to represent it admirably.
The goal is to rescue the children in each burning level and proceed to the next one. To do this you have to snake a powerful firehose that can blast both flames and baddies as you make your way to the children. You may also and often must drop your firehose and rely on your backpack with water in order to get to the further reaches of each level. There are powerups to collect, which give bonuses such as increasing the length of the hose or activating a sprinkler system that will slow the spread of fire throughout the level.
You can control either of two characters, Popo and Mimi, each with slight differences in gameplay. Popo is a bit slower but can recharge his backpack with water faster while Mimi is the other way around. Each level is timed, but you’re more likely to be overrun by flames or enemies than running out of time. The children can get singed by the fire but otherwise seem unharmed, unless you get burned carrying them, in which case they get burned too.
The game has a very catchy theme song that is also the BGM of each level.
Although it can be fun enough in single player, co-op is where the game really excels. It is very fun to coordinate with your partner as there is still only one hose in co-op. A strategy, for example, could be to have one player get the hose extension powerup that the other player can instantly use to take the hose a bit further into the flames.
Estique is a horizontal shmup with the distinct honour of being made by some of the original Compile developers, veterans of the shmup genre. This is noticeable in that it even uses some sound effects from Compile classics such as The Guardian Legend . In the game you pilot the eponymous super-robot that can transform between the bipedal mecha form that can recover damage more quickly or a sleek spaceship form that is more manoeuvrable and has a faster firing rate. Gameplay consists of carefully balancing between the two forms in the heat of battle depending on whether a more offensive or defensive approach is needed at the time.
The NES manual has a deliberately awkward English translation as a homage to the quality of writing we often encountered during the licensed era. Accordingly, the Japanese and English versions of the game are not identical, with the English version having mild censorship of the cut scenes, mimicking the restrictions that Nintendo used to impose on licensed NES games.
The game’s default difficulty is a little on the easy side, and the whole game can be completed in under an hour at the default difficulty. I get the impression that the intended difficulty is a bit higher, so you can always adjust it up for your gaming needs.
Regardless of the difficulty, the giant screen-filling boss fights are always a delight.
Why 2nd adventure, you might ask? Well, this game has an interesting history . The original adventure was written way back in 2015 to support the Arc of Cowlitz County charity. Within a couple of years, a sequel appeared and physical copies were made and distributed at the Portland Retro Gaming Expo. They aren’t made anymore, but if you’re exceedingly lucky, you might be able to nab a second-hand copy somewhere. Finally the game was uploaded to itch.io as a free download, with a nudge to donate to the charity.

SpaceX’s Starship has successfully returned to its launchpad after orbiting in space.
On a cloudy Saturday afternoon in the southern US state of Texas, a pair of large metallic arms stretched out and caught a giant in midair as it descended from the sky.
At 124 metres (407ft) tall, SpaceX’s Starship is the world’s largest and most powerful rocket, intended for travel to the Moon and Mars. Yet 22 hours after its latest blast off into space, it made history on Earth while returning, as it slipped smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2 at Starbase city in Texas.
Aerospace engineers across the globe have lauded the first-ever capture of the upper stage of a spaceship and welcomed the achievement, which signals that mega rockets could soon be fully reusable.
On Saturday, after orbiting Earth 14 times for 22.5 hours, SpaceX’s Starship emerged from thick clouds over its Starbase launch site, flipped itself to a vertical position and slowly descended into the arms on the ‘Mechazilla’ launch tower.
Like massive tweezers, the arms caught the upper stage of the spacecraft in midair, while its engines were still roaring.
The spacecraft then hooked onto the tower’s mechanical arms and shut off its engines.
The roaring sound was instantly replaced by loud cheers from watchers nearby – they had just seen for the first time in history the capture of a mega rocket.
“That was the missing link, the holy grail of spaceflight,” said SpaceX mission commentator Dan Huot. “We caught a Starship and now everything changes.”
“Congratulations to an incredible team at SpaceX!!!” SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk said.
NASA, which is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land astronauts on the Moon later this decade, also welcomed the achievement.
“It was almost magic,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said on X.
“Making more believers by the day…one step closer to [the moon],” he added.
Spacecraft returning to Earth battle gravity and a range of atmospheric factors that are nearly impossible to perfectly predict or game.
Sputnik 1, the first-ever artificial satellite sent into space, burned up while returning to Earth.
Several manned spacecraft have been destroyed while re-entering the atmosphere, killing the astronauts on board.
In April 1967, the Soviet Union’s Soyuz 1 spacecraft re-entered the atmosphere successfully, but its parachutes failed to deploy properly. Cosmonaut Vladimir Komarov died in the crash-landing near the Ural mountains. Decades later, NASA’s space shuttle Columbia disintegrated during re-entry from orbit, killing all seven astronauts on board.
In recent decades, space agencies and private firms have made major advances in safety. But many spacecraft are impossible to reuse after splashing down in the sea or on land.
Since October 2024, SpaceX has on three occasions successfully caught the boosters that propel shuttles, once they have run out of fuel and separated from the main rocket.
But until now, the main spacecraft has never been successfully caught in midair.
Soon after its return, Musk and his engineers inspected the spaceship and said that everything appeared to have worked well, including its vital heat shield.
“Ship 42 looks great!” Musk wrote on X, posting photos and videos from the launch tower.
While the capture was tricky, aerospace engineers said the upper stage catch is a big success for SpaceX.
Niharika Patel, Technical Programme Manager at Loft Orbital, a US-based space infrastructure company, told Al Jazeera that watching the catch happen was “magical.”
“Landing a rocket back on Earth is incredibly difficult and can itself be considered an engineering marvel. Now add the sheer size and weight of Starship to that equation,” she said, noting that this is also the first time the upper stage booster has been successfully caught.
“It requires incredible precision to ensure the vehicle reaches exactly the right position, withstands the extreme heat of atmospheric re-entry and executes highly controlled manoeuvres within a very tight window. And all of this happens without a pilot — it’s completely autonomous,” she added.
SpaceX has become dominant in the aerospace industry primarily because the company has been trying to slash the cost of space travel by launching reusable rocket technology and rapid, repeat engineering.
So far, its Falcon 9 rocket has launched 700 times since 2010, with its first stage being reusable and its second stage discarded into the sea.
With Starship, Musk has said he wants to create fully reusable flights that can also transport humans into space with minimum refurbishment.
“SpaceX has already significantly reduced the cost of getting to orbit through Falcon 9’s reusability. It’s super cheap and convenient to send satellites to low Earth orbit. Starship takes this a step further by being a much bigger craft and aiming for full reusability of both the booster and the upper stage,” Patel said.
She explained that a fully reusable vehicle can be rapidly refurbished and flown again, dramatically increasing frequency and reducing cost. So if Starship reaches this milestone, Patel said it would make access to space even more affordable and scalable, just as commercial aviation transformed travel by making aircraft reusable with quick turnaround times between flights.
“This is essential for the next era of space exploration, from deploying large satellite constellations and building space infrastructure to enabling sustained human exploration of the Moon and Mars,” Patel added.

2010 yılında Bodrum'da evlenen Zeynep Casalini ve Tahsin Berk'in bu evlilikten 2011 yılında Dafne adını verdikleri kızları dünyaya geldi. Ancak çift, 2016 yılında evliliklerini sonlandırarak boşandı.
Aradan geçen yıllara rağmen birbirlerinden kopmayan ikili, 2017 yılından itibaren aynı evde yaşamayı sürdürdü. Yıllar sonra ilişkilerini yeniden resmiyete dökmeye karar veren Casalini ve Berk, Bodrum'da düzenlenen törenle ikinci kez evlendi.
Çiftin nikâh töreninde en özel anlardan biri kızları Dafne'nin anne ve babasının yüzüklerini takması oldu. Ailesiyle birlikte mutluluk pozu veren Casalini, törenden kareleri sosyal medya hesabından paylaştı.
Ünlü şarkıcı paylaşımına "Anlatılmaz yaşanır" notunu düşerken, Hande Yener ve Suzan Kardeş gibi sanatçı dostları da çifti tebrik ederek mutluluk dileklerini iletti.
3 Ekim 1970 doğumlu olan Zeynep Casalini, 56 yaşında. Müzik kariyerinin yanı sıra özel hayatıyla da zaman zaman gündeme gelen şarkıcı, 2010 yılında evlendiği Tahsin Berk ile 2016'da boşanmıştı. Yıllar sonra eski eşiyle yeniden nikâh masasına oturan Casalini, ikinci kez evlendi.

Likud and Yashar, their parties, are scheduled to hold talks on Sunday, but will need to overcome major differences to work together.
Israel’s caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has renewed his appeal for a unity government with opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, casting a coalition that would keep him in power as integral to Israel’s national security.
In a video statement on Saturday, Netanyahu said his meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday “only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government”. He said such a government could “eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all” and claimed Tehran would “not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us”.
Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party and the man given the first shot to form Israel’s next government by President Isaac Herzog, called Netanyahu’s appeal a “bluff”.
“Nice try, but these tricks don’t work on me. Nor on Israel’s citizens,” Eisenkot said.
But Eisenkot confirmed that Yashar and Netanyahu’s Likud Party were talking about the proposal for a shared government.
So what, if anything, would it take for them to govern together, and what other options does Eisenkot have?
In Israel’s October 27 election, the four-party bloc led by Eisenkot won 48 of the 120 seats in the Knesset, Israel’s parliament. Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious bloc secured 53. Two Palestinian-led factions, the Joint List and Ra’am, also known as the United Arab List, won a record 19 seats between them.
Last week, Eisenkot’s bloc showed what it could do with the backing of both Palestinian-led factions, securing a 63-to-50 vote to approve the makeup of the Arrangements Committee, a panel that helps set the Knesset’s agenda while coalition talks are under way. The bloc then moved to set up temporary committees overseeing finance, foreign affairs and defence.
Eisenkot’s bloc and the two Arab-led factions hold 67 seats combined, six more than needed for an outright majority. Another possibility is a minority government backed by Ra’am’s eight lawmakers. Their support would give Eisenkot 56 votes against Netanyahu’s 53 if the Joint List’s 11 lawmakers abstained or stayed away from the confidence vote. That would allow a government to take office with fewer than 61 votes in favour, but it would depend on how all three groups voted.
But getting Eisenkot’s allies to agree to such a deal is another matter. Yair Golan, who leads the Democrats, is open to working with the Palestinian-led factions, while Yisrael Beiteinu leader Avigdor Lieberman and Together leader Naftali Bennett have rejected a coalition with Palestinians. However, both served in the government formed in 2021, when Ra’am became the first Arab party to formally join an Israeli governing coalition.
“One of Eisenkot’s main difficulties is the opposition of Avigdor Lieberman and Naftali Bennett [leaders of parties in his alliance] to relying on Arab parties,” Yasser Manna, a researcher at the Jerusalem Center for Studies on Israeli Affairs, told Al Jazeera. “This position restricts Eisenkot’s coalition options, but it does not automatically make a unity government with Netanyahu more likely. Instead, it increases the importance of negotiations with other parties, particularly the ultra-Orthodox parties.”
The other main option, which according to experts is the most likely scenario, is the Eisenkot bloc going into a coalition with both ultra-Orthodox parties in Netanyahu’s bloc, Shas and United Torah Judaism, which would take the Eisenkot bloc to 61.
Advisers from one faction of United Torah Judaism have reportedly sought a written commitment from all 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot’s bloc to pass a law exempting Jewish religious seminary students from military service and to shield it from being struck down by the High Court. Eisenkot and Lieberman are reportedly opposed to this compromise.
President Herzog gave Eisenkot until December 6 to form a government. Herzog can grant an extension of up to 14 days, which would take the deadline to December 20.
Eisenkot has left the door open to members of Netanyahu’s Likud Party and to far-right Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich’s Religious Zionist Party, provided they back a government led by Eisenkot and accept his programme.
“If members of Likud and the Religious Zionist Party truly believe this is a time for unity, as they told the president, I cannot conceive of any reason why they would not support a government under my leadership and the principles I have presented,” Eisenkot said at the ceremony where Herzog handed him the mandate.
Daniel Levy, a former Israeli peace negotiator and president of the US/Middle East Project, told Al Jazeera that agreeing to meet can serve both men politically. “The coalition formation period is about spin and distortion and trying to gain leverage,” he told Al Jazeera. “So you take a meeting to show that you were willing to talk, then say the other side made unreasonable demands.”
The two men know each other well. Eisenkot led Israel’s military from 2015 to 2019 and served as an observer in Netanyahu’s war cabinet during the first eight months of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. He left the emergency government in June 2024.
“I believe the relationship between Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot is marked by a deep crisis of trust that goes beyond political competition,” Manna said. “However, it is important to distinguish between their political disagreements and their relatively similar approaches to national security. Both prioritise military and security considerations, particularly regarding the Palestinians and Iran.”
An early test could come on Tuesday, when Eisenkot’s allies plan to replace Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana of Likud with Yashar lawmaker Matan Kahana. Eisenkot has challenged Netanyahu and Smotrich to back Kahana and allow the vote to go ahead as scheduled, saying their response would show how serious they are about cooperation.
But even if Eisenkot and Netanyahu agreed on a policy plan for government, they still have to decide who leads. “The question of who would serve as prime minister remains the central obstacle,” Manna said. “Eisenkot has so far rejected a rotation arrangement with Netanyahu.”
Meanwhile, Netanyahu is still in office as caretaker prime minister while negotiations continue. That gives him an incentive to exploit divisions among Eisenkot’s potential partners and wait for his mandate to run out, experts say.
“At this stage, Netanyahu does not necessarily need to form a new coalition himself,” Manna said. “Preventing Eisenkot from forming one may be enough to preserve his position temporarily.”
Manna said Netanyahu could also use a security crisis to increase pressure for a national government. “A renewed large-scale confrontation could increase pressure for a national unity government or shift the priorities of coalition negotiations,” he said. “At the same time, it could generate new disagreements over military decision-making, the management of the conflict, and the authority of a caretaker government.”
If talks with the ultra-Orthodox parties fail, Levy said, Eisenkot could ask his allies to choose between accepting support from the Palestinian-led parties and leaving Netanyahu in office. He could also propose a short-lived government whose immediate purpose would be to replace Netanyahu and prepare for another election.
He added that in such a scenario, Eisenkot might tell his allies to “form a government for a few months, just to get Bibi [Netanyahu] out of power and prepare for new elections”.
This would prevent Netanyahu from using “his position as prime minister to create a crisis”.

Kadir İnanır 'ın vasiyeti ve mirası üzerine süren tartışma, muhabirleri ünlülere aynı soruyu sormaya yöneltti. Son olarak konser öncesinde görüntülenen Emel Sayın'a vasiyet hazırlayıp hazırlamadığı soruldu. Usta sanatçının yanıtında en çok dikkat çeken ayrıntı ise yeğenleri oldu.
Yeğeni Levent İnanır'ın açıklamaları, Jülide Kural'ın yanıtları ve mirasçılarla ilgili iddialar her hafta dosyaya yeni bir perde ekledi. Karşılıklı açıklamalar ve dava süreciyle birlikte konu, kısa sürede magazin gündeminin en çok konuşulan başlıklarından biri haline geldi.
Bu tablo, magazin muhabirlerinin ünlülere yönelttiği soruları da değiştirdi. Son haftalarda Coşkun Sabah ve Hakkı Bulut gibi isimler de vasiyetleriyle ilgili sorulara yanıt vermişti.
Sıradaki isim Emel Sayın oldu. Konser öncesinde basın mensuplarıyla kısa bir sohbet eden usta sanatçı, soruyu geçiştirmedi.
Emel Sayın, miras meselesinin kendisini rahatsız ettiğini açıkça söyledi. Gerekçesi de netti: Ailelerin arasında zaman zaman hiç beklenmedik tatsızlıklar yaşanabiliyordu. Sanatçının sözleri, bu tür anlaşmazlıkların aile bağlarını ne kadar yıpratabileceğinin farkında olduğunu da gösterdi.
Ardından sözü kendi ailesine getirdi. 'Ben ailemin büyük bir bölümünü kaybettim zaten' diyen sanatçı, bugün en yakınında yeğenlerinin olduğunu anlattı.
'Yeğenlerim var evlat gibi sevdiğim' sözleri, açıklamanın en dikkat çeken kısmı oldu. Sayın, yeğenleriyle arasında miras yüzünden bir anlaşmazlık çıkması ihtimaline karşı da tavrını net koydu: 'Aramızda böyle bir şey olmasını asla istemem.'
Vasiyet sorusuna gelince usta sanatçının cevabı kısaydı: Bugüne kadar böyle bir hazırlık yapmayı hiç düşünmemişti.
Ancak bunun ileride bir sorun yaratacağına da inanmıyor. Sayın'a göre ailesinin yapısı buna zaten izin vermiyor: 'Miras konusunu hiç düşünmedim ama zaten bir problem olmaz.'
Sanatçı, sözlerini 'Zaten her şeyi ortak olan ve birbiriyle paylaşan bir aileyiz' diyerek tamamladı.
Yeşilçam 'ın unutulmaz filmlerinden Mavi Boncuk'ta rol alan ve Türk sanat müziğinin en sevilen seslerinden biri olan Emel Sayın, böylece Kadir İnanır dosyasıyla yeniden alevlenen miras tartışmasında kendi tavrını da ortaya koymuş oldu.
Peki ünlülerin vasiyet sorularına verdiği bu yanıtlar, miras kavgalarının önüne geçebilecek mi? Kadir İnanır dosyasında yaşananlar, konunun ne kadar hassas olduğunu bir kez daha gösteriyor.

Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.
Women's rights activists in Poland have opened what they say is the world's first delivery locker supplying abortion pills in a country with one of Europe's most restrictive abortion laws .
Known as the "Abortomat," the locker is in a building opposite the Polish parliament, in what activists say is a clear message to politicians like Donald Tusk . The Polish prime minister pledged to introduce abortion on demand up to the 12th week of pregnancy before the 2023 parliamentary election, but his coalition has been unable to agree on a common position.
Only two European Union member states, Poland and Malta, do not allow abortion on request.
In Poland, abortion is only allowed when the pregnancy is the result of a crime — rape or incest — or when it endangers the health or life of the woman.
Justyna Wydrzynska , an activist from a nonprofit organization called Abortion Dream Team, showed DW the "Abortomat" in a small room behind a tasseled portiere at Abotak, Poland's first abortion center.
Inside, the pink lighting is subdued. Glitter tassels, baubles and spotlights make it feel a bit like a disco, she said.
The "Abortomat," which opened in late September, has 22 pink lockers. To open one, a woman receives a PIN code from the organization Women Help Women after completing a medical questionnaire, which is then checked by a doctor.
Parcel lockers have sprung up like mushrooms after rain in Poland in recent years. Even the smallest villages have them.
"When you walk around Poland, vending machines are everywhere. This is our culture. People in the US have Amazon, we have vending machines for everything," said Wydrzynska.
Women in Poland who have an abortion are not criminalized. But anyone who helps them terminate a pregnancy risks up to three years in prison.
In 2023, Wydrzynska was the first activist to be convicted in Poland of helping a woman to have an abortion by sending her pills. The conviction was later overturned, and the court ordered a retrial.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Inside each compartment at the "Abortomat" is a package that normally contains two drugs, mifepristone and misoprostol, usually taken up to the 14th week of pregnancy.
Because mifepristone is not registered in Poland, the drug must be ordered from abroad where it is legal. Information on how to do this is not easy to come by, which is where Abortion Dream Team and Abotak come in. They help women find information about accessing medication, which is sent from abroad by Women Help Women, or help them to travel abroad for a termination.
Wydrzynska said she believes the "Abortomat" does not break the law because it is a machine, not a person, that is delivering the pills, although she admits she is not sure.
Dr. Sabrina Mana-Walasek, a reproductive rights lawyer representing Wydrzynska, said the legal environment for abortion pills is "complicated."
She said that although mifepristone is not registered in Poland, it is registered in the European Union and, as EU citizens, Polish women can order it and take it.
"If a woman orders pills for herself and pays for them herself, it's not a crime," she said.
The ultra-Catholic legal group Ordo Iuris disagrees and has notified the prosecutor's office that the activists are committing a crime.
"In the case of an 'Abortomat,' the actions enabling a woman to have an abortion are theoretically performed by the woman herself using the device, but the reality is that this machine is operated by people — they send the code required to open the compartment containing abortion pills, they order and procure the pills, and they restock the compartments," said Katarzyna Gesiak, director of the Ordo Iuris Center for Medical Law and Bioethics.
Wydrzynska said anti-abortion activists regularly demonstrate outside Abotak, using horns and loudspeakers to generate loud noise to annoy the center's residential neighbors and pressure the landlord to revoke their rental agreement.
At one demonstration, a woman holding an image of the Virgin Mary told DW she believes abortion "is the work of Satan."
"Abortion is evil, it's demonic, it's against the fifth Commandment, 'Thou shalt not kill,'" she said.
Earlier this year, Diana, a 25-year-old Ukrainian woman living in Warsaw , used abortion pills during her sixth week of pregnancy before the "Abortomat" started up. She got the pills using information provided by Abortion Dream Team.
"I was expecting something like a headache, stomachache, maybe vomiting, but I had nothing like that. It was just like a normal period. I didn't feel any pain. It was really easy for me," she said.
"I felt relief because I knew that it was the right choice for me. I knew that I can live my life," she added.
Another Abortion Dream Team activist, Natalia Broniarczyk, said they help about 130 women daily in Poland. About 125 of these women use pills that cost about €75 ($83), while the remainder travel to a clinic abroad.
In contrast, just 851 abortions were performed in Polish hospitals last year.
Broniarczyk is concerned about the rising support for right-wing parties ahead of next year's parliamentary election, but she's also furious at the inactivity of liberals in Tusk's coalition.
"I'm mad at the liberals because for three years, they did nothing to protect us. They lost three years and now, when we're close to an election, they are fighting for our voices and respect. People are more progressive than politicians," she said.
After taking office in 2023, Tusk's coalition, which includes left-wing and conservative partners, were unable to agree a common position and their separate bills failed to obtain parliamentary approval in 2024.
Afterwards, Tusk said abortion on request would not be possible during the current parliamentary term.
In October, however, two bills were resubmitted to the Sejm, the lower house of parliament, and were narrowly approved.
One reinstates severe irreversible fetal defects as a justification for a legal termination. This justification had been ruled illegal by the Constitutional Court in 2020 when the previous right-wing Law and Justice (PiS) -led government was in power.
The 2020 ruling led to tens of thousands of people, mostly women, taking part in street protests in towns and cities across the country, some of the largest since communism fell in 1989.
Lawmakers also approved a bill partially decriminalizing anyone who helps a woman terminate her pregnancy.
According to the results of a recent poll conducted by SW Research for Onet.pl , almost 61% of respondents said they want the country's right-wing president, Karol Nawrocki, who is backed by PiS, to sign into law the bill on the fetal defect justification.
Nawrocki opposes abortion, and both Wydrzynska and Broniarczyk think he will use his power of veto to block the bills, preventing them from becoming law.

China is forced to tread carefully as it considers hosting a meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin, and Donald Trump. While the optics are sure to favor Moscow, Beijing is risking its image on the global stage.
An unprecedented meeting between the leaders of China , Russia and the United States could be happening on the sidelines of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen this week.
China has yet to confirm that the meeting will take place. However, a Chinese Foreign Ministry official recently told the press that Beijing was "in communication" with relevant parties. In Moscow, a Kremlin representative said work on "coordination" was underway.
The clearest indication about the potential summit came from US President Donald Trump last weekend. Talking to reporters at a Florida airport, Trump said he "thinks" one of the meetings planned for APEC will be with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping .
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Despite the lack of official confirmation from either Beijing, Moscow, or Washington, the media has already dubbed the potential trilateral summit a "new Yalta," invoking the optics of the US, UK, and Soviet Union convening at the end of World War II and deciding on the new geopolitical power balance in the Crimean resort town.
At the same time, nobody seems to be quite sure what the three leaders would talk about if China agrees to host the trilateral summit at APEC.
In his brief remarks to reporters on Sunday, Trump avoided mentioning Russia's war in Ukraine when asked about the possibility of the meeting, bringing up only "Iran" and "denuclearization" as possible talking points.
The Chinese Foreign Ministry reported "no information" when questioned earlier this week about the potential substance of talks.
A three-way meeting with a photo op would be a big diplomatic win for Russia's President Putin. Since launching the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, the Kremlin chief has faced years of diplomatic boycott by Kyiv's allies , most notably the US under Trump's predecessor Joe Biden.
Putin first pitched the idea of a trilateral summit last month during a call with Trump . The Wall Street Journal has reported that Putin wanted the meeting to discuss an end to his war in Ukraine.
For the US, the president standing shoulder to shoulder with the leaders of America's foremost rivals could be a bad look, although Trump has already made a show of personally greeting both leaders with a red carpet at different points during his second term.
As host, China is in an even trickier position. While Russia and China are broadly aligned on many issues , Beijing does not want to be explicitly tied to Russia's war in Ukraine and harm China's efforts to present itself as a long-term force for global stability .
The Chinese government is also working to rebalance economic ties with the EU. The European powers would likely bristle at a summit hosted by China and discussing the war in Ukraine without Kyiv or Brussels present at the table.
"China is clearly uneasy about the possible trilateral meeting with the US and Russia, and although Beijing has shifted its position from saying nothing to admitting that the three powers are in contact, the vagueness of these declarations seems deliberate," Alicja Bachulska, Asia policy fellow at the European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR), told DW.
"Beijing is aware of the potential negative optics of the 'Yalta 2.0' framing, even if this historical comparison is inaccurate and does not reflect current geopolitical dynamics," Bachulska said.
She notes the trilateral meeting could "trigger further escalation in the already worsening relations between China and the EU" if Ukraine is discussed with no Europeans in the room.
For China, there is also little to gain in terms of optics. Images of Xi standing with Trump, the leader of Beijing's top rival, and Putin, Beijing's partner in opposing the US, could present an awkward look.
"Even if the meeting only yields a photo opportunity, it could nevertheless severely erode China's image," Bachulska added.
Putin and Xi have met some 40 times since the Chinese president came to power in 2012.
The two neighboring countries have grown especially close following the declaration of "no limits" partnership accord in early 2022. The move was announced by Xi and Putin on the sidelines of Beijing Winter Olympics, just weeks before the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
The current Russia-China ties are deeper than they have been in decades.
At the core of the axis between the two nations is a long-term strategy to contain US power while fostering an alternative global order both Moscow and Beijing can use for their own ends.
Throughout the course of the Ukraine war, which is nearing the end of its fifth year with no solution in sight, Beijing has quietly provided Russia with crucial market for energy exports, while supplying technology and so-called "dual-use" goods.
While China did not explicitly provide Russia with weapons, its exports included high-tech components that could be used for modern weapons systems like drones.
Officially, Beijing maintains neutrality on the Ukraine war and has refused to take responsibility for its outcome .
"China is more interested in reforming global governance in ways that reflect its preferences and red lines while preserving a collegial appearance," Aurelio Insisa, senior analyst at the Berlin-based Mercator Institute for China Studies (MERICS), told DW.
Even if China agrees to host the meeting, it will likely avoid framing it as three top powers making decisions for the rest of the world, according to Insisa.
"Embracing the 'G3' narrative would undermine its image as a champion of the Global South and developing countries. It is also worth noting that Beijing has shown no interest in engaging with the one pressing issue that could realistically be addressed in such a trilateral format: nuclear disarmament," he added.
In a report published in August, the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC), painted China as a "decisive enabler" of Russia's war in Ukraine.
Beijing was "converting Moscow's dependence into lasting military, technological, economic, and geopolitical advantages while avoiding the obligations of a formal alliance," according to the US body.
However, the commission also noted there were limits to Beijing's strategic support, and intelligence and security concerns remain a constraint on deeper cooperation. The report emphasizes the relationship is more of a strategic alignment than an alliance, with deep mistrust remaining in some key areas.
Russian defense firms, for instance, have accused Chinese companies of stealing intellectual property. Beijing, on the other hand, is concerned with Russia's growing strategic relationship with North Korea , which has reduced Pyongyang's dependence on China.
China and Russia also differ on nuclear doctrine. While Beijing maintains a longstanding "no first use" policy, Moscow uses nuclear threats as part of its strategy.
MERICS' analyst Insisa believes the cooperation between Russia and China will largely continue within this year's framework, including Russia providing energy and potentially transfering military technology in the "few remaining areas where it retains an advantage."
"China, in turn, will continue to supply dual-use technologies, purchase Russian energy, provide Moscow with a measure of diplomatic cover, and — more importantly — offer channels for circumventing Western sanctions," he added.
Notably, China will also get a "privileged vantage point" on how the battlefield in Ukraine is evolving land warfare.
"Strategic distrust between the two sides, particularly Russia's concerns about economic dependence on China, will continue to limit the scope of their cooperation," Insisa said.

Kitap dünyasına açılan kapınızı aralayın! En sevdiğiniz kitapları indirimli fiyatlarla keşfedin ve hayal gücünüzü genişletin.
Oyuncu Deniz Türkali ile İtalyan şarkıcı Ernesto Casalini'nin kızı olan şarkıcı Zeynep Casalini, 2010 yılında restoran işletmecisi Tahsin Berk ile Bodrum’da evlenmişti. Çift, evliliklerinden bir yıl sonra kızları Dafne'yi kucaklarına alırken, 2016 yılında yollarını ayırma kararı almıştı. Boşandıktan bir sene sonra yeniden bir araya gelen ve Bodrum'da ortaklık kuran ikili, ilişkilerini resmiyete dökerek yeniden nikah masasına oturdu.
Boşandıktan tam 10 yıl sonra eski eşi Tahsin Berk ile yeniden evlenen 56 yaşındaki Zeynep Casalini, nikahtaki şıklığıyla dikkat çekti. Üzerinde yıldızlar bulunan siyah bir mini elbise giyen Casalini, gelinliğini tül duvakla tamamladı. Nikah masasında çekilen fotoğraflarını ve kızları Dafne'yle verdikleri aile pozunu sosyal medya hesabından takipçileriyle paylaşan şarkıcı, gönderisine “Anlatılmaz yaşanır” notunu düştü.
Casalini'nin paylaşımına kısa sürede çok sayıda tebrik yorumu gelirken, sanatçı arkadaşı Hande Yener de meslektaşını “Tebrikler Zeynepçiğim, mutluluklar diliyorum” sözleriyle kutladı.
Müzik hayatına lise yıllarında başlayan Zeynep Casalini; İtalya ve İngiltere'deki çalışmalarının ardından Türkiye'ye dönerek Sezen Aksu ve Emel Müftüoğlu gibi önemli isimlerin vokalliğini yaptı. 2004 yılında çıkardığı albümle solo kariyerine adım atan sanatçı; “Duvar”, “Köprüler”, “Ne Yapsam” ve “Dokunma Bana” gibi şarkılarıyla geniş bir hayran kitlesine ulaştı. Uzun süredir gözlerden uzak bir yaşam süren Casalini, müzik çalışmalarına devam ediyor.

Nazar değmesin...” diye konuştu. Bu sözler, menajerlik açıklaması ve Lara Paşalı’nın ayna paylaşımından sonra çiftin kendi ağzından gelen ilk yanıt oldu.
Selahattin Paşalı ile eşi Lara Paşalı, el ele yürürken Gazete Magazin objektiflerine yansıdı. Son günlerde boşanacakları iddia edilen çift, kameralardan kaçmadı. Hakkındaki boşanma haberlerine şaşırdıklarını belirten ikili, evliliklerine dair kısa ama net bir yanıt verdi: 'En iyi dönemimizdeyiz... Nazar değmesin...'
Böylece kasımda yeniden alevlenen iddialara bu kez doğrudan çiftin kendi ağzından cevap gelmiş oldu.
Geçtiğimiz günlerde sosyal medyada ve çeşitli haber sitelerinde çiftin yeniden ayrılık kararı aldığı öne sürülmüştü. Selahattin Paşalı'nın menajerlik ajansı Persona Menajerlik, Instagram hikâyesinden yaptığı açıklamada bu iddiaları asılsız olarak nitelendirdi ve içeriklerin kaldırılmasını istedi; aksi halde hukuki yollara başvurulacağını duyurdu. Açıklamada 'Bugüne kadar açıklama yapılmamış olması, söz konusu iddiaların doğruluğuna işaret etmemektedir' ifadesine de yer verildi.

Birkaç gün sonra Lara Paşalı, eşiyle ayna karşısında çektikleri fotoğrafı takipçileriyle paylaştı. Çiftin el ele görüntülendiği son kareler ise dosyanın şimdilik son halkası oldu.
Paşalı çiftinin adı ilk olarak bu yılın nisan ayında boşanma iddialarıyla anılmaya başladı. Influencer Yağmur Çevik'in paylaştığı video ve ardından Ece Erken'in bir televizyon programında öne sürdüğü sözler, konuyu kısa sürede magazin gündeminin ilk sıralarına taşıdı. Lara Paşalı'nın 4 Nisan'daki doğum gününü yalnızca kızıyla kutlaması ve sosyal medya paylaşımlarını azaltması da o dönem en çok konuşulan ayrıntılar arasındaydı.

“Ömer”, “Masumiyet Müzesi”, "Kıskanmak" gibi projelerle adından söz ettiren Selahattin Paşalı, son dönemde kariyerinin yanı sıra özel hayatıyla da magazin gündeminde adından sık söz edilen oyuncular arasında yer alıyor.
16 Nisan 2022'de birlikteliklerini nikahla taçlandıran Selahattin Paşalı ile Lara Paşalı ikilisi, kızları Leyla Pera'yı aynı yıl kucaklarına alarak ilk kez anne ve baba olmanın sevincini yaşamıştı.
Örnek çiftlerden biri olarak gösterilen Paşalı ailesi, son dönemde evliliklerinde kriz yaşadıklarına yönelik iddialarla sık sık gündeme geliyor. Geçtiğimiz günlerde boşanacaklarına yönelik bir iddia ortaya atılmış, Selahattin Paşalı'nın menajerlik şirketinden ise yalanlama gelmişti.
“Son günlerde hakkımızda ortaya atılan iddialara ilişkin kısa bir açıklama yapmak isteriz. Her evlilikte zaman zaman zorlu dönemler yaşanabilir; biz de şu anda kendi içimizde bazı konuları çözmeye ve ilişkimizi daha sağlıklı bir noktaya taşımaya çalıştığımız bir süreçten geçiyoruz. Bu dönemde sessiz kalmayı tercih ettik; çünkü kişisel süreçlerimizi kendi içimizde, sakinlikle yönetmek istedik. Ancak bu sessizliğimizin yanlış anlaşılması ve farklı yorumlanması, gerçeği yansıtmayan spekülatif haberlerin artmasına neden oldu. Sürece dair kamuoyuna yansıyan detayların gerçeği yansıtmadığını özellikle belirtmek isteriz. Özel hayatımıza gösterilen hassasiyet ve anlayış için, yanımızda olan herkese teşekkür ederiz.”
Açıklamanın ardından çiften yeni bir hamle geldi. Paşalı çifti, ayrılık iddialarına sosyal medya hesaplarından yayınladıkları kareyle yanıt verdi. İkili, birlikte yer aldıkları yeni kareyi Instagram'dan paylaşarak boşanma iddialarına yanıt vermiş oldu.
Paşalı çifti aylar önce yaptıkları yazılı açıklamayla evliliklerinde zor bir süreçten geçtiklerini ve kendi içlerinde bazı konuları çözmeye çalıştıklarını açıklamıştı. Bu açıklamadan günler sonra sıkıntılı günleri geride bırakan ve birlikte tatile çıkan Lara-Selahattin Paşalı, bir kez daha ayrılık iddialarıyla gündeme gelmişti.
Geçtiğimiz günlerde bir davete tek başına katılan Selahattin Paşalı ile eşinin yine sıkıntılı günler geçirdiği hatta boşanma kararı aldığı öne sürülmüştü.

İnanır’ın hastalıkları sürecinde tedavi masrafları için bazı gayrimenkullerini sattığı iddia ediliyor.
Yeşilçam’ın usta oyuncusu Kadir İnanır, 26 Haziran’da 76 yaşında hayatını kaybetti. Vefatının ardından 23 yıllık hayat arkadaşı Jülide Kural ile ailesi arasında vasiyet ve mal varlığına ilişkin tartışmalar gündeme geldi.
İnanır’ın 9 Mayıs 2022’de doktor raporu eşliğinde hazırlattığı vasiyetinde tüm mal varlığını Jülide Kural’a bıraktığının ortaya çıkması, yeğeni Levent İnanır ile yaşanan anlaşmazlığı da alevlendirdi.
17 Aralık’ta açıklanması beklenen resmi vasiyet öncesinde aile üyeleri ile Kural arasında mal varlığı ve sanatçının özel koleksiyonlarıyla ilgili iddialar gündeme geldi. Bu süreçte usta oyuncunun banka kayıtlarında yer alan nakit varlığının 60 milyon TL olduğu öğrenildi.
Vasiyetinde de yer aldığı belirtilen 60 milyon TL dışında banka hesabında başka bir nakit varlığı bulunmadığı öne sürülen İnanır’ın, uzun yıllar devam eden hastalıkları nedeniyle yüksek tedavi masrafları yaptığı ifade ediliyor.
Usta oyuncunun özel hastanelerdeki tedavilerinin yanı sıra Küba’ya da tedavi amacıyla gittiği biliniyor.
2018’de beynine pıhtı atmadan önce akciğer kanseri süreci yaşayan İnanır’ın, bu dönemde Dalaman’daki yazlığını satarak tedavi masraflarını karşıladığı iddia ediliyor.
Daha sonraki hastalık süreçlerinde ise Ulus’taki evini sattığı öne sürülüyor. Yaşadığı Beykoz’daki evin de merhum iş insanı İsmet Acar tarafından hediye edildiği söylenmişti.
İnanır’ın vefatının hemen ardından yeğeni Levent İnanır ’ın, evdeki değerli eşyaların sayımı için polis eşliğinde eve girdiği belirtildi.
Ancak sanatçının saat, çakmak ve tespih gibi özel koleksiyonlarının kasada bulunmadığı iddiası da tutanaklara yansıdı.
Vasiyetten haberdar olan yeğenleri ve aile üyelerinin itirazlarının önemli bir bölümünün bu eşyalar ve mal varlığıyla ilgili olduğu konuşuluyor.
Banka kayıtlarında 60 milyon TL nakit varlığı bulunduğu belirtilen ve vasiyetiyle mal varlığını Jülide Kural ’a bıraktığı ifade edilen Kadir İnanır ’ın vasiyetinin resmen açıklanmasının ardından aile üyelerinin nasıl bir yol izleyeceği merak konusu.

Sabah saatlerinde köpeğini gezdirmeye çıkan Akalay, muhabirlerle ayak üstü sohbet etti. Akalay, “Her şey yolunda, birazcık hava alalım dedik ama size yakalandık” dedi.

Kadir İnanır’ın vefatının ardından ailesi ile 23 yıllık hayat arkadaşı Jülide Kural arasında mal varlığı ve vasiyet tartışmaları sürüyor. Hürriyet’in haberine göre, oyuncunun banka kayıtlarında 60 milyon TL nakit varlığı bulunuyor.
26 Haziran’da 76 yaşında hayatını kaybeden İnanır’ın, 9 Mayıs 2022’de doktor raporu eşliğinde hazırlattığı vasiyetinde tüm mal varlığını Kural’a bıraktığı belirtiliyor. Resmi vasiyetin 17 Aralık’ta açıklanması beklenirken, bu durumun yeğeni Levent İnanır ile yaşanan anlaşmazlığı da artırdığı aktarılıyor.
Haberde, 60 milyon TL’nin vasiyette de yer aldığı belirtilirken, İnanır’ın banka hesabında bunun dışında nakit varlığı bulunmadığı öne sürüldü. Uzun süren hastalıkları nedeniyle yüksek tedavi masrafları yaptığı ifade edilen oyuncu, özel hastanelerin yanı sıra Küba’ya da tedavi amacıyla gitmişti.
2018’de beynine pıhtı atmadan önce akciğer kanseri süreci yaşayan İnanır’ın, o dönemde Dalaman’daki yazlığını satarak tedavi giderlerini karşıladığı iddia ediliyor. Sonraki hastalık süreçlerinde ise Ulus’taki evini sattığı öne sürülüyor. Yaşadığı Beykoz’daki evin de merhum iş insanı İsmet Acar tarafından hediye edildiği daha önce dile getirilmişti.
İnanır’ın ölümünün hemen ardından yeğeni Levent İnanır’ın, değerli eşyaların sayımı için polis eşliğinde eve girdiği belirtildi. Oyuncunun saat, çakmak ve tespih gibi özel koleksiyonlarının kasada bulunmadığı iddiasının da tutanaklara yansıdığı aktarıldı.
Habere göre, vasiyetten haberdar olan yeğenleri ve aile üyelerinin itirazlarının önemli bir bölümünün bu eşyalar ve mal varlığıyla ilgili olduğu ifade ediliyor.
